paragraphs.heading: What it is
paragraphs.text: Reforestation means bringing back forests and woodlands that once stood but were destroyed or damaged. The loss may have come from deforestation, clearcutting or wildfires. Three important goals of reforestation programs are growing wood to harvest, helping limit climate change, and restoring ecosystems and habitats.

paragraphs.heading: Not the same as afforestation
paragraphs.text: The IPCC defines reforestation as turning land back into forest after it had been forest and then put to some other use. Afforestation is different: it means creating forest where there was none before, for example on abandoned farmland. Big programs often blur the two. China's Three Northern Protected Forest Development Program, nicknamed the Great Green Wall, began in 1978, is set to run until 2050, and aims to plant nearly 90 million acres of new forest across a 2,800-mile strip of northern China.

paragraphs.heading: Plantations
paragraphs.text: One way to reforest is to set up tree plantations, also called plantation forests. These are intensively managed, made of one or two species of the same age, planted with regular spacing, and grown mainly for production. They cover about 131 million hectares, 3% of all forest and 45% of planted forest. The other 55% of planted forests are not intensively managed and may come to look like natural forest as they mature. Between 1990 and 2015, planted forests grew from 4.1% to 7.0% of the world's forest area.

paragraphs.heading: Trees as a crop
paragraphs.text: Reforestation is not only about recovering forests lost by accident. In Finland, much forest is run by the wood products and pulp and paper industry, and trees are replanted after cutting, much like other crops. Finland's Forest Act of 1996 makes replanting after felling a legal requirement.

paragraphs.heading: Climate benefits
paragraphs.text: Using several native species can bring benefits beyond income: healthier soil, the return of local plants and animals, and the capture of 38 tons of carbon dioxide per hectare each year. Reforestation and reducing deforestation can raise carbon storage in four main ways. They can add to the volume of existing forest, pack more carbon into forests already standing, expand forest products that replace fossil fuel emissions, and cut the emissions that come from deforestation and degradation.

paragraphs.heading: Limits
paragraphs.text: Reforestation has real limits, especially as plantations. It can compete with other uses of land and carry a risk of displacement, plantations are often monocultures that reduce biodiversity, and the stored carbon may be released at some point. Planting new trees often sees up to 90% of seedlings fail. New trees also need several decades to match the carbon benefits of mature tropical forest, so reducing deforestation usually does more for the climate.

paragraphs.heading: Mending the edges
paragraphs.text: Conserving intact forests, called proforestation, pays off sooner than reforestation. Rather than planting brand-new areas, it may be better to reconnect patches of forest and restore their edges. That shields the mature core and makes the forest more resilient and longer-lasting.
